timing_disclosure: Both STATS19 and CAS H1-H3 results were known before this reporting contract was written. This is not a preregistration. It fixes deterministic summarization language only and performs no model selection, tuning, threshold adjustment or new hypothesis test.

comparison_questions.H1: Whether random-internal versus future gaps are metric-dependent rather than uniformly optimistic, with Macro-F1, QWK and fatal recall reported separately.
comparison_questions.H2: Whether weighted LightGBM versus weighted Logistic shows the same temporal-test Macro-F1 and fatal-recall directions.
comparison_questions.H3: Whether the observed mean-absolute-SHAP feature-rank agreement pattern is similar across the two separately analyzed datasets.
comparison_questions.workflow: Whether the frozen audit, temporal evaluation, ordered metrics, uncertainty and explanation-stability workflow executes on a second administrative source.

reporting_rules: Keep CAS and STATS19 records, fitted models, target definitions, absolute performance levels and uncertainty calculations separate.
Do not pool records, effect estimates, Bootstrap draws or SHAP ranks.
Do not perform a cross-dataset significance test because the datasets, feature sets, years and severity definitions are not exchangeable.
A same-sign point estimate is directional agreement only; it does not prove equality, transportability or generalizability.
An interval crossing zero is uncertainty, not equivalence.
SHAP is fitted-model attribution and not causal evidence.
Two administrative data sources do not establish cross-national or cross-domain generalizability.
